title: Desktop keyring store
whyItMatters: The keyring store holds the passwords that applications unlocked for the user: mail, chat, Wi-Fi and browser logins. On systems with automatic login the login keyring can be readable without any prompt.
source: Arch Wiki, GNOME/Keyring: collections are stored as keyring files in ~/.local/share/keyrings: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/GNOME/Keyring
notes: login.keyring holds the default collection and user.keystore the older format. The files are encrypted with the keyring password, which is empty on some auto-login installs. KDE KWallet keeps its own store in ~/.local/share/kwalletd, which this rule does not match.
